title: Breast specialist visit
what: The doctor looks at and feels your breasts and armpits. If needed, an ultrasound or mammogram is ordered.
why: If you feel a lump, have breast pain or nipple discharge, or for a routine check.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; you get the findings right away
tell_doctor: What bothers you, and since when
The date your last period started
If blood relatives had breast or ovarian cancer
If you are breastfeeding or pregnant

prepare.title: Best timing
prepare.text: Usually days 5 to 12 of your cycle, when the breasts are less swollen. After menopause, any day. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Before the visit
prepare.text: Do not put cream or deodorant on your breasts or armpits.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: A two-piece outfit is easiest. You only need to take off your top.

bring: Past breast ultrasounds and mammograms, if you have them
steps: The doctor asks about your concerns and health
The doctor looks at your breasts standing and sitting, sometimes with your arms raised
Then your breasts and armpits are felt while you lie down
The doctor explains the findings and orders tests if needed
feel: If your breasts are tender, it may be uncomfortable. Tell the doctor
after: If an ultrasound or mammogram was ordered, book it on a good day of your cycle
Check your breasts yourself once a month at home. Your doctor will show you how

faq.q: At what age should I start seeing a breast specialist?
faq.a: Regular routine checks are usually advised, and mammograms from age 40. If you have symptoms, at any age.

faq.q: Is a breast lump always dangerous?
faq.a: No. Most lumps are benign. But you must show it to a doctor.

reminders.text: Breast specialist visit tomorrow. Bring past scans, and do not use cream or deodorant in the morning.
